measurement: close before print to close after first full session following

names.notes: Reported Q2 FY2027 after close 2026-09-01: non-GAAP EPS $7.04 vs ~$4.88 consensus (beat by ~44%), revenue $47.0B vs ~$45.0B consensus (beat, +58% y/y). FY27 revenue guidance raised by $25B to $192B; EPS guidance raised to $25.50. Shares gapped up 8.7% at the open and kept climbing through the session to close +15.81%, breaking the 11.5% unsigned expected move. The Neutral / No Edge call is a miss under the below-expected-move convention (moved hard, panel had no view), though it lands inside its wide 5.7-34.4% band. The red-team's specific reversal case -- a HP-style margin-compression selloff on the memory cost cycle despite a headline beat -- did not fire; the $51.3B AI-server backlog dominated instead, exactly the scenario the same persona flagged as the top risk to its own bearish call. The stage-2 preliminary read (+20, bullish) called the direction correctly.

Reported Q2 FY2027 before open 2026-09-02: non-GAAP EPS $0.11 vs $0.10 consensus (beat), revenue $213.7M vs ~$215.6M consensus (miss, ~-0.9%), subscription revenue +3% y/y. Q3 revenue and EPS guidance both came in below consensus; FY27 subscription outlook raised only modestly, total revenue outlook held flat. Shares opened roughly flat, rallied intraday to +2.8%, then reversed hard to close at the day's low, -8.55% -- breaking the 6.8% unsigned expected move (no options-implied move existed to size against). The Neutral / No Edge call is a miss under the below-expected-move convention. The red-team's specific reversal case -- 'a beat is not enough a third year running because cRPO/guide stay soft' -- is exactly what fired: cRPO growth stayed low-single-digit and Q3 guidance disappointed, with no forward inflection to offset it. The stage-2 preliminary read (-25, bearish) called the direction correctly and, notably, was the only source (panel included) that anticipated the guide would be the problem rather than the print itself.

Reported Q2 FY2027 before open 2026-09-02: revenue $554.1M vs ~$570.3M consensus (miss, ~-2.8%, driven by the planned Calvin Klein/Tommy Hilfiger license exits), GAAP EPS $0.46 well above a cited GAAP-basis estimate of $0.17 (estimate basis uncertain -- flagged lower confidence). FY27 guidance raised on net income/EPS despite the revenue miss; completed the Marc Jacobs acquisition. Shares opened roughly flat but sold off through the session to close -11.50% near the day's low. The stage-2 preliminary read (-20, bearish) called the direction correctly.

Reported Q2 FY2027 after close 2026-09-01: non-GAAP EPS $0.24 vs $0.18 consensus (beat), revenue $286.3M vs ~$273.1M consensus (beat, +21% y/y), both FY27 revenue and EPS guidance raised above consensus. Shares gapped up 22.4% at the open, spiked to +23.2% intraday, then faded to close +9.98% -- roughly half the peak gain, a real intraday give-back a close-to-close number understates. The stage-2 preliminary read (-20, bearish) called the wrong direction on a clean beat-and-raise.

Reported Q2 FY2027 after close 2026-09-01: non-GAAP EPS $1.90 vs $1.61 consensus (beat, +18%), revenue $771.8M vs ~$733.7M consensus (beat, +5.2%, +30% y/y). FY27 revenue outlook raised to $2.99-3.03B. Despite beating every headline estimate and raising guidance, shares opened down and drifted lower all session to close -13.54% -- the market read the Q3/Atlas growth outlook as no acceleration. The stage-2 preliminary read (+10, mildly bullish) called the wrong direction; this is the sharpest 'beat everything, still fall double digits' case across all three runs scored today.

Reported Q1 FY2027 after close 2026-09-01: non-GAAP EPS $1.20 vs $1.17 consensus (beat), revenue $479M vs ~$471.8M consensus (beat, +115% y/y, 7th straight triple-digit growth quarter), FY27 outlook reaffirmed. Shares still opened down and fell further through the session to close -20.04%, driven by gross-margin compression (64.5% GAAP gross margin, down from 68.2% the prior quarter) rather than anything in the headline numbers. The stage-2 preliminary read (+10, mildly bullish) called the wrong direction -- the largest single-name miss (by magnitude) across all three runs scored today, and on a name that beat every consensus line.
